summary: Go Write covers the basic create/overwrite path, shared ReadState, parent directory creation, atomic write, structured patch generation, team-memory secret rejection, history hooks, optional LSP hooks, and several alignment tests. It is still not TS-exact. The highest-risk gaps are model-visible/structured output shape, strict input and permission semantics, stale-write robustness, post-write ReadState lifecycle, line-ending and encoding policy, symlink/file-mode behavior, un-wired skill/LSP/editor lifecycle hooks, file-history metadata, remote git diff shape, and Go-only notebook/documentation/memory analytics behavior. This report is analysis-only; no tests were run.

gaps.title: Go returns model-visible JSON that does not match the TS Write data/result contract
gaps.description: TS Write returns structured data with exactly the outputSchema fields `type`, `filePath`, `content`, `structuredPatch`, `originalFile`, and optional `gitDiff`, then maps that data to short model-visible success text. Go serializes an expanded JSON object directly into ToolResult.Content, omits top-level `content`, adds Go-only fields (`isNew`, `bytes`, `lineCount`, `status`, `path`, `diagnostics`, `userModified`, `metadata`, `warning`, `remoteGitDiff`), and therefore changes both API transcript content and programmatic result shape.

ts_evidence.note: TS outputSchema defines only type, filePath, content, structuredPatch, originalFile, and optional gitDiff.
TS update result data includes content and optional gitDiff under the outputSchema names.
TS create result data includes content, empty structuredPatch, originalFile null, and optional gitDiff.
TS maps successful tool results to short strings like `File created successfully at:` or `The file ... has been updated successfully.`
The TS executor maps typed result data through mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam before adding the tool_result block.

go_evidence.note: Go builds an output map with type, filePath, isNew, bytes, lineCount, structuredPatch, status, path, diagnostics, userModified, and metadata, but no top-level content.
Go adds originalFile, optional documentation warning, memory analytics side effects, and remoteGitDiff.
Go returns ResponseJSON(out), making the expanded JSON object the model-visible tool result content.
ResponseJSON marshals arbitrary content into ToolResult.Content as a JSON string.
Registry copies ToolResult.Content directly into the ToolResultBlock sent onward.
Anthropic provider sends ToolResultBlock.Content as the tool_result text when no ContentBlocks are present.
Current tests assert Go-only isNew/bytes/lineCount fields instead of the TS outputSchema shape.

gaps.impact: Replay fixtures, SDK consumers, transcript compaction, UI summaries, and the model itself see different Write results than they would in TS.

gaps.title: Go does not enforce TS strict-object input validation or the same path normalization boundary
gaps.description: TS uses z.strictObject, describes file_path as absolute, and backfills observable input by expanding `~` and relative paths before hook/permission allowlists see it. Go's shared JSONSchema cannot express additionalProperties:false, parseInputOrError uses json.Unmarshal which ignores unknown keys, and Write trims file_path then resolves with filepath.Abs without shell-style `~` expansion. This permits TS-invalid inputs and changes path identity for whitespace or tilde paths.

ts_evidence.note: TS input schema is z.strictObject with required file_path and content.
TS backfillObservableInput expands file_path so hooks/allowlists cannot be bypassed through ~ or relative paths.
TS tool schemas can carry arbitrary JSON schema fields beyond type/properties.

go_evidence.note: Go JSONSchema has only Type, Properties, Required, and Description; no additionalProperties field.
Generic parsing marshals the input and json.Unmarshal's into a struct, which ignores unknown object keys by default.
FileWriteInput has only file_path and content fields, so unknown keys are silently dropped.
Go schema publishes required fields but cannot express TS strictness.
Go trims file_path, checks non-empty, and separately checks content presence.
Go canonicalizes through filepath.Abs/Clean, which does not expand `~` like TS expandPath.

gaps.impact: The same tool_use can be rejected in TS but accepted in Go, or target a different path after Go-only trimming/normalization.

gaps.title: Write permission decisions are not equivalent to TS checkWritePermissionForTool
gaps.description: TS Write delegates to the edit permission system, checks deny rules during validateInput, handles ask/allow/session .claude exceptions, path safety, suggestions, and working-directory decisions. Go Write only enforces AllowedDirs/symlink-safe path containment internally, while the loop has a generic optional PermissionHandler and a separate protected-path SafetyCheck. That does not reproduce TS's per-tool updatedInput, rule source, suggestion, acceptEdits, and deny/ask/allow ordering semantics.

ts_evidence.note: TS Write checkPermissions calls checkWritePermissionForTool.
TS validateInput rejects edit deny rules before filesystem work.
checkWritePermissionForTool first checks deny rules against original and resolved paths.
TS handles editable internal paths, session-scoped .claude allow rules, and protected-path safety suggestions before allow rules.
TS checks ask rules, acceptEdits working-directory mode, allow rules, and default ask with suggestions.

go_evidence.note: Go Write's internal permission boundary is checkAllowedPath against AllowedDirs.
checkAllowedPath resolves symlinks and rejects paths outside allowed directories; it does not model TS permission rules or suggestions.
Go loop permission requests contain only session, tool name, input, mode, and AvoidPrompts.
PermissionHandler is optional; nil means allow-all execution at the loop layer.
Go has protected-path hard denies for Write, but this is a separate bypass-immune safety check rather than TS's ask/suggestion-based edit permission decision.

gaps.impact: Write calls can be allowed, denied, or prompted differently from TS, especially for .claude paths, protected config paths, outside-working-directory paths, and rule-based allow/ask/deny settings.

gaps.title: Go lacks TS's full-read content fallback for benign mtime changes
gaps.description: TS rejects stale writes when mtime moved after the last read, but for full reads it compares current normalized content to the stored read content to avoid false positives from cloud sync, antivirus, or timestamp-only touches. Current Go Write rejects immediately when mtime is newer than the ReadState timestamp, even if the current bytes still match the read snapshot.

ts_evidence.note: TS checks lastRead and lastWriteTime, then permits full-read cases when meta.content equals lastRead.content despite timestamp movement.
TS identifies full reads by offset and limit being undefined before comparing content.

go_evidence.note: Go requires a ReadState entry and rejects partial views.
Go immediately returns the modified-since-read error when isFileStale is true.
isFileStale is only mtime.UnixMilli() > entry.TimestampMs.
Current stale-read test asserts mtime-newer rejection with identical stored content and does not cover the TS fallback.

gaps.impact: Go can force unnecessary rereads and block valid TS writes after timestamp-only filesystem activity.

gaps.title: Post-write ReadState can participate in Go Read dedup where TS prevents it
gaps.description: TS Write refreshes readFileState after a successful write so future writes are not stale, but it sets offset and limit to undefined. TS Read dedup requires offset to be defined, so a post-write state entry cannot produce file_unchanged. Go Write stores a ReadFileEntry with zero Offset/Limit and LastTool='Write'; Go Read dedup compares only offset, limit, and mtime, so a subsequent Read can incorrectly dedup against the post-write state entry.

ts_evidence.note: TS Write refreshes readFileState with content, timestamp, and offset/limit undefined.
TS file_unchanged dedup requires existingState.offset !== undefined, so post-write entries are excluded.

go_evidence.note: Go Read dedup checks Offset, Limit, and TimestampMs but does not inspect LastTool/source.
Go Write stores Content, TimestampMs, IsPartialView=false, LastTool='Write', and leaves Offset/Limit at zero.
ReadFileEntry has Offset, Limit, IsPartialView, Content, LastTool, Encoding, and BOM, but no explicit undefined offset representation.
The Read parity report independently documents that Go dedups broader state than TS, including Write-stamped entries.

gaps.impact: A Read immediately after Write may suppress file content in Go where TS would re-read and show the new file contents.

gaps.title: Go rewrites model-supplied line endings and preserves extra encodings that TS does not
gaps.description: TS Write deliberately stops preserving the old file's line-ending convention and writes the model-supplied content as-is, using the detected file encoding. Go normalizes CRLF and bare CR to LF before writing. Go also detects and re-encodes UTF-16BE, BOM-less UTF-16, Latin-1, and UTF-8 BOM metadata, whereas TS detectEncodingForResolvedPath only returns utf16le for UTF-16LE BOM and otherwise utf8. These choices may be useful, but exact byte output can differ from TS for CRLF payloads and non-TS-detected encodings.

ts_evidence.note: TS chooses meta encoding and calls writeTextContent with 'LF' while comments state the model-sent line endings are explicit and should not be rewritten.
writeTextContent only rewrites line endings when endings === 'CRLF'; for 'LF' it writes content unchanged.
TS encoding detection returns utf16le only for FF FE BOM and utf8 for UTF-8 BOM or all other non-empty files.

go_evidence.note: Go normalizes content to LF before encoding/writing.
normalizeLineEndingsToLF replaces both CRLF and bare CR with LF.
Go detects UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16LE/BE BOM, BOM-less UTF-16 heuristics, valid UTF-8, and Latin-1 fallback.
Go re-encodes content for non-UTF8/BOM encodings recorded in ReadState.
Current tests assert UTF-16LE BOM preservation; there are no parity tests for CRLF payload preservation versus TS.

gaps.impact: The same Write call can produce different bytes on disk, especially for CRLF content, bare-CR content, UTF-16BE, BOM-less UTF-16, Latin-1, or UTF-8 BOM files.

gaps.title: Go rejects symlink writes and resets existing file mode instead of matching TS write-through and permission preservation
gaps.description: TS's low-level writer detects symlinks, resolves the target, writes through to the target, and preserves the existing target mode on atomic temp replacement. Go refuses to overwrite any symlink target and always calls atomicWriteFile with 0644, so overwriting an executable or custom-mode file can change permissions.

ts_evidence.note: TS readlinkSync detects symlinks and resolves targetPath for write-through behavior.
TS stats the target, records targetMode, and chmods the temp file to preserve existing permissions before rename.
TS fallback write also targets the resolved targetPath.

go_evidence.note: Go uses Lstat and returns an error when the target path itself is a symlink.
Go calls atomicWriteFile with fixed permission 0644.
atomicWriteFile chmods the temp file or fallback target to the provided perm.
Current tests assert symlink rejection and unchanged real target.

gaps.impact: Go has stricter symlink safety but diverges from TS-visible behavior; file permission bits can also change after overwrites.

gaps.title: Write does not trigger TS skill discovery and conditional skill activation in Go
gaps.description: TS Write discovers skill directories for the written path, records dynamicSkillDirTriggers for display, adds skill directories in the background, and activates conditional skills for matching paths. Go has comparable skill discovery machinery for Read, but FileWriteTool has no SkillManager field and SetupRegistry only wires FileReadTool.SkillManager.

ts_evidence.note: TS Write discovers skill dirs, stores dynamicSkillDirTriggers, calls addSkillDirectories, and activates conditional skills for the path.
ToolUseContext carries dynamicSkillDirTriggers and discovered skill state used by tools.

go_evidence.note: FileWriteTool fields include no SkillManager or skill-trigger state.
Go has DiscoverSkillDirsForPaths for read-triggered skill discovery.
FileReadTool invokes skill discovery and conditional activation after reads.
SetupRegistry wires the shared SkillTool manager into AgentTool, TeamManager, and FileReadTool only.

gaps.impact: Creating or rewriting files that should surface nearby/conditional skills can update the filesystem in Go without activating the same skill context TS would attach.

gaps.title: Go's LSP and editor notifications are optional shims, not the wired TS lifecycle
gaps.description: TS Write always calls diagnosticTracker.beforeFileEdited, clears delivered diagnostics for the file, notifies the shared LSP manager with didChange and didSave when available, and calls notifyVscodeFileUpdated with old and new content. Go has optional LSP/DiagnosticsTracker/VSCodeNotifier fields and tests for manually injected fakes, but SetupRegistry wires Write to NewNoopLSPDiagnoser with no DiagnosticsTracker or VSCodeNotifier. The LSPTool's manager is constructed separately and not shared with Write; the VSCode notifier callback receives only new content, so it cannot reproduce the TS diff notification payload.

ts_evidence.note: TS calls diagnosticTracker.beforeFileEdited before writing.
TS clears delivered diagnostics and sends changeFile/saveFile to the LSP manager.
TS calls notifyVscodeFileUpdated(fullFilePath, oldContent, content).

go_evidence.note: Go exposes optional LSP, DiagnosticsTracker, and VSCodeNotifier fields.
Go invokes optional DidChange/DidSave/Diagnose and diagnostics tracker after write.
Go VSCodeNotifier receives only absPath and new content.
SetupRegistry constructs FileWriteTool with LSP: NewNoopLSPDiagnoser and no DiagnosticsTracker or VSCodeNotifier.
ENABLE_LSP_TOOL registers a separate LSPTool with its own LSPServerManager; it is not injected into Write.
Current tests prove the optional hooks work only when fakes are manually injected.

gaps.impact: The default Go runtime does not keep editor/LSP/diagnostic state in sync with Write the way TS does, and Go can surface diagnostics in a different channel from TS.

gaps.title: File history tracking differs in timing, gating, and identity metadata
gaps.description: TS conditionally tracks file history before the atomic read-modify-write section using updateFileHistoryState and parentMessage.uuid, so backups are correlated with the tool use/message even if later staleness fails. Go appends a JSONL entry after a successful write, ignores failures, generates an EditID when missing, has no visible feature gate, and does not carry the parent message UUID or AppState-style updateFileHistoryState semantics.

ts_evidence.note: TS calls fileHistoryTrackEdit(updateFileHistoryState, fullFilePath, parentMessage.uuid) before the staleness check when fileHistoryEnabled() is true.
TS call receives parentMessage and updateFileHistoryState in the tool context.

go_evidence.note: Go HistoryStore is an optional FileWriteTool field; nil disables history.
Go writes history after the file write succeeds using Before, After, Tool, and timestamp.
Go FileHistoryEntry has EditID but TrackEdit generates a new UUID when it is empty.
SetupRegistry always constructs a FileHistoryStore at <cwd>/.claude/file-history and injects it into Write.
Current tests only assert a JSONL file exists after successful Write, not TS timing, feature gate, or parent message ID correlation.

gaps.impact: Undo/replay/file-history consumers can observe different history entries, missing message correlation, and different behavior on stale-write failures.

gaps.title: Remote git diff shape, gating, and analytics differ
gaps.description: TS attaches optional `gitDiff` as a structured ToolUseDiff only when both CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE and the `tengu_quartz_lantern` feature are enabled, and logs diff computation analytics. Go uses a package-global SetRemoteGitDiffEnabled toggle, shells out to `git diff`, truncates a string, and places it under `remoteGitDiff`; no SetupRegistry wiring or analytics equivalent is visible.

ts_evidence.note: TS checks CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE plus growthbook flag, fetches fetchSingleFileGitDiff, assigns gitDiff, and logs tengu_tool_use_diff_computed.
TS outputSchema names the optional diff field gitDiff.
ToolUseDiff is a structured diff type rather than a raw string.

go_evidence.note: Go uses a package-global remoteGitDiffEnabled boolean controlled by SetRemoteGitDiffEnabled.
Go returns a raw git diff string, with optional truncation, or empty string.
Go attaches the diff under remoteGitDiff, not gitDiff.
SetupRegistry constructs FileWriteTool but does not wire the remote diff flag from CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE or a feature resolver.

gaps.impact: Remote UI and SDK consumers expecting TS `gitDiff` cannot consume Go Write's diff payload without special-casing, and feature-gated behavior can diverge.

gaps.title: Go adds runtime notebook/documentation/memory behaviors that TS Write does not enforce
gaps.description: TS prompt text tells the model to prefer NotebookEdit/Edit and not create documentation unless explicitly requested, but FileWriteTool itself does not reject .ipynb writes or emit a warning field for Markdown creation. TS analytics logs only paths ending in CLAUDE.md. Go rejects .ipynb writes, adds warning to new Markdown/README/CHANGELOG JSON payloads, logs AGENTS.md and local variants through isClaudeMemoryWritePath, and invalidates a Go memory mtime cache. These may be desirable product policies, but they are not exact TS runtime parity.

ts_evidence.note: TS prompt guidance says Write overwrites files, prefers Edit, and says never create docs unless requested; this is guidance, not call-time validation.
TS validateInput checks team memory secrets, edit deny rules, UNC path filesystem avoidance, and read-before-write/stale state; it has no .ipynb or documentation warning branch.
TS logs tengu_write_claudemd only when fullFilePath ends with /CLAUDE.md.

go_evidence.note: Go rejects .ipynb writes and tells callers to use NotebookEdit.
Go adds warning to successful new documentation file results.
Go logs CLAUDE/AGENTS memory writes and invalidates the memory mtime cache.
Go treats claude.md, agents.md, agents.local.md, and claude.local.md as memory write targets.
Current tests assert .ipynb rejection.
Current tests assert documentation warning output.

gaps.impact: Go can reject or annotate Write calls that TS would execute, and memory analytics/cache behavior differs for AGENTS.md-style files.

gaps.title: Current Write tests lock several Go-only behaviors and miss key TS parity edges
gaps.description: Go has useful tests for core writes, read-before-overwrite, stale rejection, partial read rejection, symlink rejection, payload counts, plan mode, allowed dirs, history, and optional LSP hooks. However, tests currently assert Go-only output fields and policies, contain stale comments claiming older missing fields, and do not cover TS-compatible short tool_result text, top-level content/gitDiff data shape, strict unknown-key rejection, tilde expansion, permission-rule ordering, stale content fallback, post-write Read dedup suppression, CRLF preservation, file mode preservation, default registry LSP/skill wiring, file-history message correlation, or remote diff gating.

ts_evidence.note: TS strict input and output schemas define the contract tests should pin.
TS stale fallback and post-write readFileState behavior are important lifecycle edges.
TS symlink and mode preservation are filesystem edges missing from current Go parity tests.

go_evidence.note: Current tests assert isNew/bytes/lineCount and warning fields, which are not TS outputSchema fields.
Header comments still describe missing HistoryStore/LSP fields even though current FileWriteTool has them.
LSP/VSCode tests use manually injected fakes and do not verify default registry wiring.
Current tests assert stale mtime rejection and symlink rejection rather than TS fallback/write-through parity.

gaps.impact: Future changes can pass existing Go tests while moving farther from TS, or can be blocked by tests that intentionally assert Go-only policy.

candidate_tasks.title: Align Write output data and model-visible tool_result with TS
candidate_tasks.description: Introduce a TS-shaped Write result contract and separate internal metadata from the model-visible tool_result text. The successful model-visible result should be the TS short create/update sentence, while structured data should expose type, filePath, content, structuredPatch, originalFile, and optional gitDiff using TS names.
dependencies: Coordinate with any existing loop/tool-result structured-output work so ToolResult can carry TS-style data without forcing JSON into Content.
WRITE-TASK-011 should supply the final gitDiff shape.
acceptance: Create returns structured data with type=create, filePath, content, structuredPatch=[], originalFile=null, and optional gitDiff only.
Update returns structured data with type=update, filePath, content, non-empty structuredPatch when content changes, originalFile, and optional gitDiff only.
The model-visible tool_result content matches TS text for create and update.

Go-only fields isNew, bytes, lineCount, status, path, diagnostics, warning, remoteGitDiff, userModified, and metadata are absent from the TS-shaped Write data unless explicitly moved to non-model internal metadata.
candidate_tasks.notes: This is the largest integration task because current ToolResult is text-first. Keep the compatibility layer narrow and avoid changing unrelated tools unless a shared structured-output carrier is already planned.

candidate_tasks.title: Make Write input validation strict and path expansion TS-compatible

dependencies: If strict parsing is generalized in parse.go, audit other tools before switching defaults.
acceptance: Write rejects unknown top-level keys.
Write rejects missing or non-string file_path/content with TS-like validation errors.
Write expands ~ and relative paths consistently before permission, read-state, and filesystem checks.
Write no longer silently changes target identity by trimming leading/trailing file_path whitespace unless TS does the same.

candidate_tasks.title: Reproduce TS edit permission decision semantics for Write
candidate_tasks.description: Add a Go Write permission path equivalent to checkWritePermissionForTool, including deny/ask/allow ordering, resolved-path checks, internal editable paths, .claude session allow exceptions, acceptEdits behavior, protected-path ask/suggestions, and updated input propagation.
dependencies: WRITE-TASK-002 should land first so permission checks see TS-expanded paths.
Coordinate with Bash/Edit/NotebookEdit permission parity because TS uses the shared Edit permission namespace.

acceptEdits mode allows writes in allowed working directories.
Protected paths follow TS ask/suggestion semantics unless a deliberate Go safety override is documented separately.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement TS stale-write content fallback
candidate_tasks.description: When an existing file's mtime is newer than the stored read timestamp, permit Write if the prior read was a full read and current normalized content still equals the ReadState snapshot. Keep partial reads and missing snapshots rejected.
dependencies: None, but coordinate with WRITE-TASK-006 for line-ending normalization of the comparison.
acceptance: Existing file with newer mtime but unchanged full-read content is writable.
Existing file with newer mtime and changed content remains rejected.
Partial-read entries remain rejected.
The error text for true stale writes matches TS.

candidate_tasks.title: Prevent post-write ReadState entries from satisfying Read file_unchanged dedup
candidate_tasks.description: Represent TS's undefined offset/limit or use LastTool/source semantics so Write-refreshed state can support future Edit/Write staleness checks without causing a subsequent Read to return file_unchanged.
dependencies: Coordinate with the Read parity task for READ-GAP-002 to avoid duplicate fixes.
acceptance: Read immediately after Write returns file contents, not file_unchanged.

Edit/NotebookEdit post-write entries follow the same non-dedup policy.
file_unchanged text matches TS once Read parity is addressed.
